Jacob. The grandson of Abraham and son of Isaac, remembered as the patriarch whose name was changed to Israel, meaning "he who strives with God."

His name change to Israel came after wrestling with a divine being at the Jabbok ford, a pivotal moment of spiritual wrestling and blessing. A figure of cunning and transformation, Jacob tricked his twin brother Esau out of his birthright by trading lentil stew, and later deceived his father Isaac to steal Esau's blessing.

His twelve sons became the founders of the twelve tribes of Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Dan, Naphtali, Gad, Asher, Issachar, Zebulun, Joseph, and Benjamin. He worked fourteen years for his uncle Laban to marry his beloved wife Rachel, being tricked into first marrying Leah. His favorite son was Joseph, whose coat of many colors sparked jealousy among the other sons.

After years of separation and conflict, Jacob reconciled with his brother Esau. His life story moves from deception to spiritual encounter, culminating in his covenant relationship with God. Jacob's story is found primarily in the book of Genesis, chapters twenty-five through fifty.
